newsitem.title: USA: Ryerson Tull Q1 market share rises.
newsitem.headline: Ryerson Tull Q1 market share rises.

text.p: Ryerson Tull Inc, a metal distributor and processor, said Monday its gross profit per ton fell to $212 in the first quarter from $232 a year ago, reflecting weak industry-wide metals prices.
Earlier, Ryerson reported first quarter net income of $16.6 million or $0.42 a share, down from year-ago results of $22.4 million or $0.57 a share.
Ryerson said its first-quarter market share rose to an estimated 9.7 percent from 9.2 percent a year ago, based on Steel Service Center Institute data.
"This market share growth, combined with strong service center industry shipment levels, produced an 11 percent increase in tons shipped," Neil Novich, president, said in a statement.
First quarter expenses per ton dropped to $165 from $175 a year ago, he added.
Volume gains and cost control efforts, however, were offset by the decline in the gross profit, Ryerson said.
